MikroTik Burst Calculator

Plan RouterOS queue burst — how long it lasts, when it comes back, what's misconfigured — and watch a simulation of the speed a client actually gets. Generates simple queue, PPP / Hotspot rate-limit and queue tree config.

Split view
ParameterUploadDownloadWhat it does
max-limitNormal speed cap (MIR) whenever burst is off.
burst-limitReplaces max-limit while burst is allowed.
burst-thresholdBurst is allowed while the average rate stays below this.
burst-timeWindow the average is measured over — not how long the burst lasts.
limit-atGuaranteed rate (CIR) when the parent is congested. Doesn't change burst timing.
Want bursts ofseconds?
rate-limit

Rates take RouterOS units: 512k, 1500k, 20M, 1G. Times: 16s, 1m.

Step-by-step table (as in the MikroTik docs)

Every burst-time ÷ 16 the router averages the traffic of the last burst-time; burst is allowed while that average is below burst-threshold, and while it is, burst-limit replaces max-limit. The simulated client always takes everything the queue allows, like the docs' example — real TCP ramps up, so actual bursts can look shorter. MikroTik's own example tables have a few arithmetic slips (the 16 s example's 18 s row adds up to 1625 kbps, not 1500), so from there this simulation, which applies the rule exactly, differs from the printed numbers.

RouterOS config

Simple queues and pairs are upload/download; in a rate-limit string rx is the client's upload and tx its download. The queue-tree lines need mangle rules that set those packet marks.
